text:
Samir (CS): FYI Customer reported repeated/duplicate completions after an SSE disconnect. They see partial output, then reconnect, and the model generates the tail again so they end up with duplicated tokens and double billing. Filing here for triage.
Elaine (Customer): repro steps I have: open EventSource -> receive streaming chunks -> network blip -> browser reconnects automatically -> on resume we get the last 2 chunks again plus new content. Costs doubled for that request id: req_0x9f3. Not using any idempotency header right now.
Samir (CS): Customer attached server logs (snippet) complaining about resume_token mismatch. Example SSE chunk:
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq":12,"resume_token":"rt_abc123","generation_checksum":"sha1:5df"}

event: done
data: {"generation_id":"gen_7f1"}
```
Then after reconnect we see a new chunk with same text but new generation_id:
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq":12,"resume_token":"rt_def456","generation_checksum":"sha1:5df"}
```
Elaine (Customer): We also captured browser side: EventSource reconnect sends Last-Event-ID header with seq=12 and the client then issues a fresh POST without any idempotency key because our app code didn't add one.
Nina (Eng Infra): Thanks. First pass hypothesis: resume_token is rotating on auth/session refresh. Client resumes using old seq which server treats as a new generation because token->generation mapping lost; runtime starts a new generation using same prompt prefix -> duplicate output. Also possible: resume token TTL < client reconnect backoff.
Jordan (Runtime): Agreed. Runtime currently doesn't attach a stable generation_id to the prefix keyspace that survives token rotation. We usually dedupe by idempotency_key on request creation, but streaming reconnections without idempotency key fall through.
Samir (CS): Customer wants a workaround ASAP to avoid billing duplicates.
Jordan (Runtime): Short-term mitigation we can push (low-risk): when we emit chunk events, include a stable "generation_id" meta field and persist minimal mapping {generation_id -> checksum, final_token}. On reconnect if client supplies Last-Event-ID or resume_token we check generation_id checksum and if matches, resume without re-running. If resume_token rotated we can accept old tokens for short TTL if they map to a generation_id.
Nina (Eng Infra): Implementation notes: add an in-memory sticky cache (LRU) keyed by resume_token and generation_id for 5 minutes, and check at reconnect path. This will cover most mobile/browser blips. We'll also log a special marker so CS can audit duplicates.
Samir (CS): Can we instruct the customer with a quick workaround?
Nina (Eng Infra): Yes. Ask them to send an "X-Idempotency-Key" header on the original POST that produces the stream. If they reconnect, client should replay that same header on the POST used to resume (or include it in a resume request). Server will check and return prior partials instead of re-generating. Example client snippet:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Idempotency-Key: 33b7e" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"...","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```
Samir (CS): Good. Add that to the support reply. Also practical repro steps for eng:
1) start streaming curl client (no idempotency key).
2) after some chunks, kill network (tcpkill) to simulate blip.
3) rotate server resume_token (simulate auth refresh) and allow client to reconnect with Last-Event-ID=seq.
4) observe if runtime spawns new generation or resumes.
Use these greps: `grep req_0x9f3 | jq '.generation_id, .resume_token'` to correlate.
Jordan (Runtime): Quick patch idea (runtime): emit a meta line early: `event: meta
data: {"generation_id":"gen_7f1","checksum":"sha1:5df"}`. On resume, client must send resume headers including Last-Event-ID. Runtime will check mapping by generation_id first. If matches, resume the same generator state (KV cache) instead of re-roll.
Nina (Eng Infra): I'll open a ticket to add a 5-minute sticky mapping and a short-lived accept list for rotated resume_tokens. We'll also surface a duplicate-detection metric in Console: `stream.resume.duplicate_count`.
Samir (CS): Jordan/Nina, ETA on the sticky mapping and meta field? Customer is sensitive (billed twice).
Jordan (Runtime): I can add the meta field and generator_id propagation this week (minor runtime change). Sticky mapping in infra needs a small config and can go next week.
Nina (Eng Infra): I'll aim to have a mitigation rollout to canary in 48-72 hours.
Samir (CS): Great. I'll tell the customer the temporary client-side workaround (X-Idempotency-Key + echo it on resume) and that we're working on server-side dedupe.
Elaine (Customer): Thanks — we'll add the Idempotency header and report back if duplicates stop. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
resume-bot: Logged ticket RT-2248 for "SSE resume token rotation -> duplicate generations" and linked this thread.
Samir (CS): Action items: Samir send workaround + repro steps to customer; Nina open infra ticket + graph; Jordan add meta/generation_id change; follow-up in 72h.
